newsitem.title: USA: Simpson custody battle decision expected - report.
newsitem.headline: Simpson custody battle decision expected - report.

text.p: A judge was expected to issue a ruling on Friday in O.J. Simpson's custody battle over his two young children by Nicole Brown Simpson, CNN reported.

Sydney, 11, and Justin, 8, have lived with the parents of Simpson's slain ex-wife since shortly after her death on June 12, 1994. Simpson, who was acquitted in October, 1995 in the murders of his ex-wife and her friend and is embroiled in a civil wrongful death lawsuit, now wants the children back.

Closing arguments in the custody case ended earlier this month in Orange County family court. Judge Nancy Wieben Stock took the matter "under submission" and said she would issue a written decision later.
Lawyers in the case and a court spokeswoman were not immediately available to comment on the CNN report.

Attorneys for Louis and Juditha Brown, the children's maternal grandparents, have contended that Simpson -- who signed over temporary guardianship to them after his June 17, 1994, arrest -- is an unfit parent, citing allegations that he beat and threatened his ex-wife.

But Simpson's lawyers have argued that he has a right to full custody as the biological father. Simpson reportedly has also expressed concern that living with the Browns, who are white, his children are not being properly instructed in their black heritage.
